## 7 Discussion and Limitations

The results in §6 measure internal consistency rather than
correctness. Check 1 tests compliance with a ruleset the system authored itself;
Check 2 tests coverage against a concept-skill map that Map Extraction produced and
that is not independently validated. Neither consults an external standard, and for
most of the run history the same model served as both Generator and Eval, so
self-preference effects cannot be excluded in general. The ablation of
§6.3 offers one data point against them: with Eval on
claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-6’s first attempts passed Check 1 at least as often
as claude-sonnet-5’s in every chapter, the opposite of what self-preference would
predict, though the difference is not significant. We therefore report no agreement
statistic against an expert-authored Q-matrix, and claim no psychometric validity
for the released data. Most consequentially, we never fit a CDM: the paper’s premise
is that the Q-matrix blocks cognitive diagnosis, but we hold no student response data
and report no model fit, leaving the released mapping a candidate structure of
untested diagnostic utility. Nor do we establish that the released granularity suits
any particular model: §5.2.4 reports the per-chapter attribute
counts and what they imply for different model families, but which granularity is
diagnostically appropriate is itself an empirical question we have not addressed.
The efficiency argument is likewise asserted rather than measured: $1.19 per chapter
counts API spend only, excludes all human review time, and has no manual baseline
beside it. Two further threats bound the results. The escalation rate’s fall from 84.2% to
8.5% coincides with a single configuration boundary that changed the verification
gate, the models, the attempt budget and the retry loop together
(§6.3); a scoped ablation rules out the Generator’s model upgrade
as the cause and is consistent with a partial budget effect, but leaves the rest
unattributed, so no part of the fall can be credited to the system having learned
anything. And we run no architectural ablation, so nothing establishes that eleven
single-responsibility agents outperform one well-prompted call, though the choice
follows a broader pattern of decomposing educational and knowledge-graph tasks into
specialized agents rather than one generalist call (Santos et al., 2026; Zhao et al.,
2025b).

Within the released artifact, the verification guarantee covers concept-skill mapping
only. None of L1, L2, or L3 passes through the Check 1/Check 2/repair loop: each
issues a single LLM call and writes straight into the confirmed CSV, so all 7,448
prerequisite edges lack that guarantee, and 1,442 of them (19.4%) are not
model-judged at all but inferred in code from skill-level relations. On the one
